findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher can never fail the grant check: inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: The new matcher is supposed to assert that an access-token ID like "onrtac:<uuid>" carries the expected grant shortcut. In the 6-char prefix the grant shortcut sits at indexes 4-5 (2 chars session type + 2 chars token type + 2 chars grant type), but the code reads items[0].substring(3, 5), i.e. the second token-type character plus the first grant character. On top of that the condition is inverted: it returns false (no match) when the extracted text EQUALS expectedGrantShortcut, so a token with the wrong grant type is always accepted and expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken now assert nothing about the grant. The check should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also, a prefix shorter than 5 characters makes substring(3,5) throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of cleanly reporting a non-match.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom OAuth2 grant type providers at server startup
findings.body: Adding an abstract method to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface means any existing third-party/custom grant-type provider compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError as soon as getShortcut() is invoked on it. That invocation happens eagerly for every registered grant factory in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), i.e. during server boot, so upgrading with an existing custom grant provider deployed makes Keycloak fail to start with an obscure error. A default method (for example returning the "na"/unknown shortcut, or deriving a shortcut from the provider id) would keep existing implementations working.

findings.title: Javadoc suggests ~3-letter shortcuts but the token-id decoder hard-requires exactly 2 characters per field
findings.body: The javadoc of getShortcut() says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires the encoded prefix before ':' to be exactly 6 characters and slices it as 2/2/2, throwing IllegalArgumentException otherwise. A grant factory that follows the documentation and returns a 3-letter (or 1-letter) shortcut will produce access-token IDs that the decoder later rejects, and the duplicate-shortcut validation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() does not check shortcut length, so nothing catches this at startup. The contract should state that shortcuts must be exactly two characters and postInit() should validate that, or the encoding/parsing should be made length-agnostic.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: The line `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` repeats the grantType check (with the rawTokenId message) instead of checking rawTokenId. As a result an AccessTokenContext can be constructed with a null rawTokenId, and encodeTokenId() will then silently produce a token ID ending in "...:null" via string concatenation instead of failing fast.

findings.title: Only the standard token-exchange provider records the grant type; other exchange flows mint tokens with "na" grant
findings.body: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set on the client session context only in StandardTokenExchangeProvider. The legacy (V1) token exchange provider and the other V2 exchange providers (subject impersonation, federated) create access tokens through the same TokenManager paths without ever setting this attribute, so access tokens they issue are encoded with the "na" (unknown) grant shortcut instead of "te". Since a stated motivation of this PR is to reliably know the grant type for token-exchange use cases (#37117), the signal will be missing/misleading for those exchange flows.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes via NullPointerException from the unwired factory, not via the intended validation
findings.body: The test builds DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory by calling init() and hand-populating grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts, but never calls postInit(), so the sessionFactory field stays null. Decoding "ofrtac:5678" enters the lazy-refresh branch of getGrantTypeByShortcut(), which dereferences sessionFactory and throws NullPointerException; the broad catch (RuntimeException) then lets the test pass. The intended IllegalArgumentException path ("Unknown value 'ac' for grant type") and the lazy map-refresh logic in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut are therefore never actually exercised, and the test would still pass if that logic were broken or removed.
